title: A Compass for the Lantern
premise: In 1859, on a storm-battered headland, widowed lighthouse keeper Silas Blackwood has spent seven years keeping his light burning and his past buried. When census taker Ada Quill arrives and recognizes the name he abandoned, Silas's carefully erased life resurfaces: a promise made to his late wife's brother, Tomas, now branded an enemy of the Crown, to shelter him if he ever reached the coast. As government orders come to decommission the lighthouse and sweep the shore for fugitives, Silas must choose between the law that pays him and the family that needs him. With Ada's reluctant help and the found community of wreckers, fishermen, and outcasts who owe him their lives, Silas smuggles Tomas aboard a departing ship at dawn—sacrificing his post, his name, and finally his invisibility, but gaining a family worth being seen for.
about_author: L. M. Blackwood is the pen name of a former maritime archivist who spent a decade cataloguing lighthouse keepers' logs along the northern coast. Their fiction draws on the marginalia of those records—the debts, disguises, and quiet mercies that official histories leave out.

chapters.title: The Weight of Glass
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Opening in the routine of tending the lamp during the first great storm, we learn of his wife Maren's death and his habit of measuring life in portable things. Emotional beat: grief disguised as competence.

chapters.title: A Question Too Many
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Census taker Ada Quill arrives between storms; her questions about household members unsettle him when she asks after 'any kin expected.' He lies, but she notices the lie. Emotional beat: the first crack in his invisibility.

chapters.title: What the Sea Returns
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Walking the coast road, Ada reflects on the names people give her versus the ones they keep, and finds wreckage bearing a foreign maker's mark—evidence of ships the harbor master doesn't report. Emotional beat: curiosity hardening into suspicion.

chapters.title: The Promise in Peacetime
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter, Silas's POV. Seven years earlier, Maren extracts a deathbed promise: if her brother Tomas ever comes, Silas will hide him, no questions, no borders. Emotional beat: love as an unpaid debt.

chapters.title: Orders Come
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. An official notice arrives: the lighthouse will be decommissioned at season's end, replaced by an automated light, and all coastal residents will be registered against a watch list. Emotional beat: the ground shifting under a man who thought he owned nothing worth taking.

chapters.title: The Wreckers' Ledger
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Ada interviews the fishing village and discovers an informal economy of rescue—Silas has pulled drowning men from the water for years, asking nothing. Emotional beat: her suspicion complicated by admiration.

chapters.title: A Knock at Low Tide
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. A half-drowned stranger appears in his boathouse: Tomas, alive, hunted, carrying Maren's old locket. The promise comes due. Emotional beat: terror and tenderness colliding.

chapters.title: Enemy of the Crown
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. His account of exile, imprisonment, and escape, and why he risked the sea to reach the one man who owed him nothing by blood. Emotional beat: shame transformed into desperate hope.

chapters.title: Counting Heads
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Ordered to return and verify the keeper's household before the watch list closes, Ada must decide whether to report the extra man she glimpsed. Emotional beat: duty pulling against conscience.

chapters.title: Bread and Salt
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Silas feeds Tomas, teaches him the lamp mechanism, and begins treating him as family rather than burden—but knows every shared meal is evidence. Emotional beat: found family forming under threat.

chapters.title: The Harbor Master's Price
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Seeking passage, Tomas approaches a smuggler captain who names an impossible price—and hints he already knows who Tomas is. Emotional beat: hope curdling into blackmail.

chapters.title: Storm Season
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. The worst storm in a generation strikes; the automated replacement isn't ready, and only Silas's hand-kept light saves a mail packet. Emotional beat: proof of his worth arriving exactly when he's been declared worthless.

chapters.title: What Ada Saw
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. During the storm Ada shelters at the lighthouse and sees Tomas plainly. Silas begs her silence; she leaves without answering. Emotional beat: the moment her report could become a death sentence.

chapters.title: The Blank Line
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Alone with her forms, Ada writes the household count—and leaves one line blank. Her superiors notice. Emotional beat: crossing the line from observer to accomplice.

chapters.title: Watch List
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Soldiers arrive to survey the headland ahead of decommissioning; Tomas hides in the lamp room while Silas performs normalcy above them both. Emotional beat: claustrophobic dread.

chapters.title: The Captain's Leverage
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. The smuggler captain, pressured by authorities hunting a fugitive, offers to trade Tomas's location for his own amnesty. Emotional beat: betrayal as arithmetic.

chapters.title: A Debt Among Thieves
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Ada confronts the captain with what she knows of his own unreported cargo, forcing a fragile bargain: passage for Tomas in exchange for mutual silence. Emotional beat: justice negotiated outside any courtroom.

chapters.title: The Last Firing
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Decommission day: officials extinguish his flame and seal the tower. Silas hands over his keys knowing Tomas hides below in the oil store. Emotional beat: surrender as cover.

chapters.title: Night Watch
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs interwoven. The escape plan assembles through the sealed night—Ada forging transit papers, the village covering tracks, Silas moving Tomas along cliffs he knows blind. Emotional beat: a whole invisible community becoming visible in purpose.

chapters.title: Before the Morning Tide
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. At the cove, soldiers intercept the boat; Silas claims Tomas is his own son, giving the lie his dead wife's face. A tense standoff breaks when the captain weighs anchor early. Emotional beat: the climax—identity offered as sacrifice.

chapters.title: What Can Be Carried
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Watching the ship fade, Silas carries away only Maren's locket's twin, which Tomas returned, and Ada's blank census line. He is dismissed, unnamed, unemployed. Emotional beat: loss measured against a promise kept.

chapters.title: A Compass for the Lantern
chapters.summary: Ada's POV, closing. Months later, Ada finds Silas living openly in the village under his true name, teaching boys the lamp craft; a letter arrives from across the sea in Tomas's hand. Emotional beat: inheritance redefined—not property passed down, but belonging chosen.
